subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: Should SMS overload preserve a truthful failure response, or should OpenClaw durably queue validated callbacks before acknowledging them, instead of returning HTTP 200 while discarding them?
rationale: HTTP success is a provider-level acceptance signal, so changing that signal while dropping the message is a delivery-policy choice automation cannot safely resolve.

options.title: Keep truthful rejection
options.body: Retain HTTP 429 for callbacks not accepted for processing and leave durable overload handling for a separate bounded design.

options.title: Queue before acknowledging
options.body: Persist validated callbacks in a bounded queue and return HTTP 200 only after acceptance for later dispatch.

options.title: Approve acknowledgment-and-drop
options.body: Explicitly accept provider-level success for discarded messages and document the resulting loss and disabled fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep truthful rejection
recommendation.body: Retain HTTP 429 for callbacks not accepted for processing and leave durable overload handling for a separate bounded design.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current quota split and documented fail-closed callback behavior on this exact path.
